additions: H1: Visual Studio Code 1.148
Release date: November 25, 2026 Stable
H2: Downloads for 1.148.0

Keep agent work moving, even when you step away. This week, chat responses start faster and active agents can keep their hosts awake. Give a task its own Dev Container, and reclaim disk space from old worktrees without switching windows.
Keep agents going (Preview): Prevent idle sleep of the systemon supported hosts while agents work.
Worktree cleanup: Reclaim disk space from inactive agent worktrees on remote hosts.
Sandbox profiles (Experimental): Tailor sandbox rules to each remote agent host with reusable profiles.
Create Dev Containers (Experimental): Give an agent an isolated Linux workspace without writing a container configuration.
Agent chat performance: Spend less time waiting for Agent Host chat responses to begin.
H2: Agents
H3: Improved chat performance
This week we've made several improvements to the performance of chat in the Agent Host. On average you can expect to see responses begin 30% faster than in our previous Stable version.

We appreciate your feedback as we've transitioned our harness to the Agent Host, and the performance difference compared to the old harness was a recurring topic of discussion. With this release, we see chat start times within ~5% of those of the old harness, and we will continue to find ways to further improve in upcoming releases.

can prevent idle sleep while an Agent Host chat is working. Configure it on the host machine, not the client. See the AI settings reference for its modes and platform limitations.
In the Agents window, you can alternatively use the Experimental sharing setup form to compare connection methods before starting sharing.
Find the remote host and select Connect on its row.
Select the existing session from the sessions list in the Agents window to continue the conversation.

You can also create and manage standalone Dev Containers here, on this computer or a connected host. Unlike a connection to an existing machine, each standalone container provides a new workspace with its files in a Docker volume.
The This Computer section manages how this computer is shared. It requires

, which is on by default. With the default sharing controls, choose GitHub Environments (when available), Dev Tunnels, or Off, or select Rename Sharing Name to change the name other clients see. Alternatively, use the Experimental sharing setup form to choose a method before applying it. Local sessions continue to run on this computer whether sharing is on or off.

The Other environments table lists known SSH hosts, dev tunnels, and WSL distributions on Windows. When support for GitHub environments is available and enabled, it also lists your registered machines, including offline ones. These are user-shared machines, not the managed environments used by cloud sessions.

Run Agents: Manage Remote Environments from the Command Palette (⇧⌘P (Windows, Linux Ctrl+Shift+P)), or select Manage Remote Environments from Remote Connections (antenna icon) in the title bar or the sessions list More Actions (...) menu.
To compare connection methods before starting sharing, enable
sessions.chat.remoteEnvironments.sharingSetup
. This Experimental setting is off by default and requires the This Computer section to be enabled.
On the host machine:
Open remote environment management.
In This Computer, select Share This Computer.
Choose a connection method and review the sharing name. Selecting a method alone doesn't start sharing.
Select Start Sharing and complete any sign-in or confirmation prompts.

From the client machine, continue an existing session or start a remote session. Sharing enables access to the host's supported sessions, tools, and workspace resources. Review remote connection security before starting sharing.
To switch methods, select Change Connection Type next to Stop Sharing, choose another method, then select Switch Method. Switching stops sharing with the current method before starting the new one.
To end remote access, select Stop Sharing. This doesn't stop running agent tasks. If a sharing change fails, select Open Sharing Log in the error message for details.

additions: For a Git workspace, use the isolation dropdown above the input to choose where the agent edits files:
Branch: Work directly in the selected folder. If you choose another local branch, switching branches requires a clean working tree.

New Worktree: Work in a separate directory and branch. Use the branch picker to choose the base branch before sending the prompt. Choosing a base branch doesn't switch the branch in your active workspace.
For the folder-versus-worktree comparison, Git requirements, and dependency setup, see Work with agents in worktrees. To change the initial choice, configure isolation defaults.
Worktrees isolate working files, not the agent's access to your machine or external services. Review the permission and sandboxing considerations before starting a task.
To reclaim disk space from inactive or leftover worktrees, run Chat: Open Worktree Cleanup. The shared cleanup procedure covers both windows, local and remote worktrees, and what is preserved.

Use a Dev Container to run the agent with tools and dependencies inside a container rather than directly on its host. Containers can run on this computer or on a configured SSH, Tunnel, or WSL host. These workflows aren't supported in the VS Code for the Web.
Choose the starting point that fits your task:
Use your project's Dev Container to work with its existing files and configuration.
Create a container without a project for a fresh Ubuntu workspace.
Ask the agent to continue in a new container to hand off a task to a new session.
Create a standalone Ubuntu container when you need a fresh workspace without an existing project folder or devcontainer.json. Its files stay in a Docker volume on the machine that runs the container.
Before starting, install and run Docker on the intended host, with its CLI on PATH. For a remote host, connect to it first. For WSL, Docker must be available inside the distribution.
